problem: Home currently lists accessible Identity Projects and Workspaces but omits the applications connected to those Identity Projects, so users cannot quickly find the sign-in experiences they can access.
invariants: Identity remains the authority for applications, project membership, application status, and lifecycle.
The application directory is scoped to Identity Projects visible to the signed-in Identity account; Platform Workspace membership grants no Identity visibility.
Only application directory fields needed for discovery are returned: application id, name, key, URL, status, and owning Identity Project id, name, slug, mode, and status.
Client identifiers, secrets, callbacks, authentication configuration, and other private application configuration are never returned to the browser.
The directory is read-only and does not create a Platform copy of Identity application state.

context.outcome: Home gives a signed-in user a concise directory of Identity applications available through the user's Identity Project memberships, alongside the existing Identity Project and Workspace directories.
context.scope: Global Home is scoped to the authenticated Identity account. Identity determines which projects and application summaries the account can read; Workspace membership is not consulted.

useCases.name: Read the Identity application directory
preconditions: The caller has a valid signed-in Identity bearer token
Identity resolves the caller to an account
useCases.result: Return safe application discovery summaries whose owning Identity Projects are visible to the caller, without mutating Identity or Platform state.

policies: Identity API authenticates the current user and filters the directory by active Identity Project membership; Identity system administrators retain the same all-project visibility as the Identity project directory.
The Platform API forwards the caller's Identity bearer token and maps the response to an explicit summary contract; it does not use service credentials or Workspace membership to expand access.
The browser receives no client identifiers, credential material, callback URLs, or application authentication configuration.
Identity access denial is reported as access-needed; upstream failure is reported as unavailable; successful results remain isolated from Workspace directory failures.
invariants: Only active Identity Project memberships determine regular-user application visibility.
Each returned application carries its owning Identity Project summary so the user can identify its source and open that project in Identity Console.
The application directory is a live read and stores no mirrored application data.

readModels.name: IdentityApplicationDirectory
readModels.purpose: Render accessible applications on Home with a project context, status, and safe destination URL.
readModels.source: A single Identity API read using the signed-in user's bearer token, projected into a typed Platform API and BFF summary.

boundaries.domainOwner: talred-identity owns application membership authorization and application state; talred-starter PlatformWorkspaceResource owns only the read integration and transport mapping.
boundaries.persistence: Identity API reads current Identity Hosted Applications and active project memberships; Platform persists no application projection.
boundaries.api: Versioned Identity API exposes an authenticated application-directory read; versioned Platform API exposes a typed directory and availability state.
boundaries.bff: talred-starter Nuxt server route proxies the authenticated Platform API with the caller's Identity session scope.
boundaries.client: Starter Home renders a responsive Applications section with loading, unavailable, empty, and available states, plus a link to the owning Identity Project.
boundaries.identity: Identity API authenticates the bearer, filters by active Identity Project membership, and remains authoritative for every returned application field.
boundaries.runtime: Reuse the existing local Identity, Platform API, and Starter web services; no new service, secret, or provider is required.

acceptanceCriteria: Home renders application summaries returned by Identity for projects visible to the current account.
A user without membership in an Identity Project cannot see its applications, even if the user is a member of a Platform Workspace linked to that project.
Application summaries include owning project context and only the explicitly approved discovery fields.
Identity access denial and upstream failure have distinct localized states; a Workspace loading failure does not erase a successful application directory and vice versa.
Application cards link to the owning Identity Project in Identity Console and do not offer Platform-side lifecycle or configuration actions.
English and French Home copy cover the Applications section, loading, empty, unavailable, access-needed, status, and project context.
decisions: Expose a dedicated bulk Identity application-directory read instead of making one Identity detail request per project; keep the data live and avoid N+1 upstream requests.
For regular users, align application visibility with Identity's active project membership directory; return only safe discovery metadata and leave configuration access in Identity Console.
Keep application directory availability independent from the existing project and workspace reads so one unavailable source does not blank the others.
